Problem statement 1: AI- based predictive waste management.
(Traditional garbage collection follows fixed routes and schedules,
causing unnecessary trips, fuel wastage, and garbage-bin overflow. There is
a need for a smart system that can monitor bin levels in real time, predict
when bins will be full, and optimize garbage truck routes using IoT and AI.)
Abstract:
AI-Based Predictive Waste Management is a smart city solution designed to
make garbage collection more efficient, economical, and environmentally
friendly. The project combines IoT sensors, wireless communication,
Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and smart route planning to
improve the traditional waste collection process. In the proposed system,
ultrasonic sensors are installed inside garbage bins to measure the distance
between the sensor and the garbage. From this measurement, the system can
determine the approximate fill level of each bin in real time. The collected
information is then transmitted to a cloud server using battery-friendly
wireless technologies such as LoRaWAN or 4G. The collected waste-level data
is analyzed using Machine Learning techniques. The system considers
previous waste-filling patterns, festivals, weekends, holidays, weather
conditions, and the type of location because these factors can affect the
amount of waste generated. Machine Learning models such as LSTM and
XGBoost can be used to predict when a garbage bin is likely to become full.
After predicting which bins require collection, the system performs dynamic
route planning. Instead of sending a garbage truck to every bin, it selects
only the bins that need collection and calculates an efficient route. The route
can also consider traffic conditions, road closures, and the carrying
capacity of the truck, helping the driver complete the collection with less
unnecessary travel. The main objective of this project is to prevent garbage-
bin overflow, reduce unnecessary truck trips, save fuel and operating
costs, reduce travel distance, and improve cleanliness in cities. The
system replaces fixed and routine garbage collection with a more intelligent,
data-driven approach. In the future, the system can be extended with AI-
based waste sorting cameras, solar-powered smart bins, and
autonomous waste-collection vehicles.

Problem statement 2: AI- based fake identity and document screening
system.
(Traditional identity verification is often slow and may fail to detect
tampered documents, fake identities, and AI-generated deepfakes. This
creates a need for an AI-based system that can quickly verify documents,
match faces, detect spoofing, and identify fraudulent identities.)
Abstract:
AI Fake Identity & Document Screening is an AI-based security system
designed to detect fake identities, tampered documents, deepfake faces,
and other forms of identity fraud. The project uses Computer Vision,
Optical Character Recognition (OCR), Deep Learning, and biometric
verification to make the identity verification process faster and more secure.
The system first captures the user's identity document, selfie, and live
video. It checks the document using AI-based forensic techniques to identify
changes in text, fonts, layouts, image quality, holograms, and other security
features. OCR is used to extract information from the document and compare
it with QR codes or machine-readable information to find mismatched details.
For face verification, the system uses ArcFace and 3D vision models to
compare the user's selfie with the photograph on the identity document. Anti-
spoofing techniques are used to detect attempts involving screens, printed
photos, masks, or deepfake video. Finally, all verification results are
combined by a central decision system to provide an instant Pass or Reject
decision. The main goal of the project is to reduce identity fraud, improve
verification speed, and replace error-prone manual checking with an
automated AI-based screening process. The system can be useful in areas such
as digital banking, visa processing, and remote user onboarding.

Problem Statement 3: AI powered Geofencing- intelligence location
based services.
(Traditional geofencing uses fixed boundaries and GPS tracking, which can
cause false alerts and high battery usage. There is a need for an AI-powered
geofencing system that can understand user movement, adjust boundaries
dynamically, and provide more accurate location-based alerts.)
Abstract:
AI-Powered Geofencing is an intelligent location-based system that uses
Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, GPS, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and
mobile sensors to create smart and dynamic virtual boundaries. Unlike
traditional geofencing, the proposed system can change the boundary
according to real-time conditions such as user speed, traffic, weather, and
movement patterns.The system collects location and sensor data from
mobile or IoT devices. AI analyzes information such as speed, direction,
stopping time, and previous movement patterns to understand the user's
activity and possible intention. Based on this information, the virtual
boundary can automatically expand or reduce when required.The system also
reduces false alerts caused by poor GPS signals or temporary boundary
crossings. It can provide useful actions such as sending alerts, controlling
devices, protecting restricted areas, or starting automated tasks.The
main aim of this project is to make geofencing more accurate, intelligent,
battery-efficient, and useful in real-world applications such as vehicle
safety, industrial safety, smart cities, and autonomous drones.

questions.question: Which component enables Transformers to process all tokens in parallel rather than sequentially?
questions.explanation: Self-attention computes pairwise token affinities in parallel across the sequence, bypassing the sequential bottleneck of RNNs.

questions.question: What is the purpose of temperature parameter T in language model decoding?
options: Scales logits before softmax to modulate output randomness
questions.explanation: Dividing logits by temperature T before softmax affects the probability distribution: lower T concentrates probability on top tokens, higher T flattens it.

notes.title: Transformer Architecture Foundations
notes.content: Key components of the Transformer: Multi-Head Self-Attention, Scaled Dot-Product Attention, Positional Encodings (Sinusoidal & RoPE), Feed-Forward Networks with GELU activations, and Layer Normalization (Pre-LN vs Post-LN). Self-attention calculates queries Q, keys K, and values V with softmax((QK^T)/sqrt(d_k))V.
notes.summary: Transformers rely on scaled dot-product self-attention mechanisms and positional encodings to process sequential context in parallel rather than recurrently.

flashcards.front: What is the formula for Scaled Dot-Product Attention?
flashcards.back: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax( (Q * K^T) / sqrt(d_k) ) * V
To prevent the dot products from growing excessively large for large dimensions, which would push softmax into regions with vanishingly small gradients.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of Positional Encodings?
flashcards.back: Because self-attention is permutation-invariant, positional encodings inject sequence order information.
